svg.text: Threads 0–15 read their first-half float4 of weight_piece[i]: which banks they hit
Shared memory has 32 banks, 4 bytes each; column c of a piece row is in bank c mod 32. Each round reads one word per bank.
(a) 8 neighbouring columns per thread (before run 4): thread n starts at column 8n
(b) two halves, 64 apart (now): thread n starts at column 4n
all 32 banks busy: 2 rounds, the fewest 64 floats can take
Threads 16–31, the warp's other half, make the next 8 rows and the same columns, so they read the same addresses:
shared memory sends one read to both halves at once. 16 float4 are 64 floats; one round reads 32 words, so 2 rounds is
the least. In (a), columns 0, 32, 64 and 96 all fall in banks 0–3, and banks 4–7 are never used: 4 rounds. ncu counted
40% of all shared memory reads as such repeats. (b) is run 4: one change of index math, 23% off every forward.
